# The appointments Tlāloc made — and who is keeping them

One myth is a story. A cycle of myths is a specification. Read Tlāloc's cycle in order and the industries fall out of it one by one.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Tlāloc
- **Pantheon:** Nahuatl
- **Domain of influence:** Rain, Water, Lightning
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Energy & Natural World
- **Strongest seat:** Agriculture, Food & Harvest
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 258 of 287

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest — through *The Abduction of Xōchiquetzal*

Colonial accounts make Xōchiquetzal, the young goddess of flowers, weaving, and sexual love, the wife of Tlāloc before Tezcatlipoca abducted her for her beauty (Leyenda de los Soles).  The tradition bound the green growing world to the water that sustains it.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Rain decides the harvest; the most propitiated farmer’s god of Mesoamerica.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. That is the cycle working: story becomes duty, duty becomes trade.

### Meteorology & Weather Intelligence — through *The Destruction of the Fourth Sun*

The Fourth Sun, the Sun of Water (4-Water), was ruled by Tlāloc's consort Chalchiuhtlicue, and it ended in a flood that lasted fifty-two years.  Humans were transformed into fish; the cosmos had to be remade.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Rain and lightning together; the agricultural forecast made divine.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

### Freshwater & Hydrology — through *The Children of the Mountain*

Child sacrifices were offered to Tlāloc, especially during drought.  The children, selected for their beauty, were believed to become Tlaloque who would bring rain from the mountain caves.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Rain is the supply side of every water system.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. That is the cycle working: story becomes duty, duty becomes trade.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Tlāloc's myths turn on a single terrifying truth: the same rain that feeds can also drown, strike, or rot. He is generous and punitive in equal measure.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

The atlas is not a horoscope. Seats are earned from the sources — argued, weighted, published — and every one of them can be challenged at the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). A match that cannot survive an argument does not survive review. That is the whole trick: the patterns are claims, and claims can be tested.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in agriculture, food & harvest, meteorology & weather intelligence, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/tlaloc/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
